newsitem.title: GERMANY: S&P rates Gerling claims-paying ability AA-.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Gerling claims-paying ability AA-.

text.p: Rating agency Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had assigned an "AA-" claims-paying ability rating to Gerling-Konzern Allgemeine Versicherungs-AG (GKA).
S&P said the rating was based on GKA's "excellent global business position, improved capitalisation and good underwriting performance in a soft domestic market."

S&P said GKA was a major, core part of the Gerling group which also includes large global reinsurer Gerling-Konzern Globale Rueckversicherungs AG, an investment management company and operations writing life, health, credit and leagal expenses insurance.
The agency described GKA as a leading player in the German and international commercial insurance markets with a strong reputation for expertise and innovation.
It was also a household name for insurance in Germany even though its penetration of the personal lines market was minimal apart from employer sponsored schemes.
Gerling benefited from synergies with other companies in the Gerling group in the areas of reinsurance, marketing and risk control, S&P said.

Its risk portfolio was well diversified by line of business and geographically and unsually in the German market, GKA obtained 85-90 percent of its domestic business through its own specialised sales force numbering 2000.

"Following a capital injection of 154 million marks in 1996 and favourable operating results in 1995/96, GKA's capitalisation is considered to be excellent: available capital is now over 165 percent of that required for GKA's volume and mix of business, according to Standard & Poor's model," S&P said.
S&P said GKA would expand strongly in its international markets as the German market was expected to be relatively flat.
"In order to compete globally, Standard & Poor's expects GKA to maintain solvency at its current excellent level," S&P said.
